thread:
Maya: After the INC-2026-42 writeup, let's create a compact program to close the hygiene gaps for staged rollouts. I'd like three parallel workstreams: rollout policy, runtime rollback hook, and telemetry + drills. Can we assign owners and short timelines?
Omar: +1. Prefer small, testable increments. We should avoid heavy config explosion.
Priya: I'll take rollout policy. Early sketch: default sampling 5%, max tenant exposure 8%, and a mandatory hold at 20% for manual review. Add a grace window and an allowlist for opt-in auto-rollback.
Lina: I'll own the runtime hook. Thinking: expose a minimal API that can be triggered by the canary monitor. Example CLI to trigger rollback: `./rcli rollout cancel --deployment ${DEPLOYMENT_ID} --reason "canary-failed"`
Kevin: I'll handle telemetry. Need to add model-health (KL divergence vs baseline), token-error counts (by error code), request path, and upstream latency histogram. Also need a canary label on traces.
Sam: SRE wants a circuit-breaker that redirects traffic to a safe variant and pins resources so the canary doesn't steal capacity. Also add a fast-read-only mode for the control plane during incidents.
dev-bot: Reminder: add these as actions: https://go/actions/pm/INC-2026-42/ai.
Maya: Proposal for auto-rollback criteria (statistical + threshold): require a minimum of 300 canary requests and a 95% confidence interval showing error-rate uplift > 2x baseline AND absolute increase > 1.5%. If both hold for 2 consecutive 1m windows, fire rollback. Sketch: ```yaml
auto_rollback:
  enabled: false
  min_samples: 300
  ratio_threshold: 2.0
  abs_threshold: 0.015
  consecutive_windows: 2
  window_seconds: 60
  allowlist: ["team-a", "beta-tenants"]
```
Priya: That statistical approach looks good. Add an abort if model-quality metrics (KLdiv) exceed a soft threshold even if error-rate is stable.
Lina: For the runtime changes I'll add a fallback hook that calls the orchestrator to swap traffic, then emit an event to the audit log. Draft PR: https://git/repo/runtime/pulls/112
Omar: Can we ensure the rollback path is idempotent and callable via both automated monitors and manual CLI? Also implement a short cooldown to avoid flip-flopping.
Sam: Agreed. Cooldown suggestion: 10m. We'll also add a quota per-tenant for concurrent rollbacks to avoid saturation.
Kevin: Dashboards I'll produce: canary-summary (pass/fail), error-rate uplifts, KL divergence trend, rollback events timeline, and recent config changes. I'll also add alert rules: P95 latency up 40% OR error-rate uplift > 1.5% for 2m -> notify oncall + trigger canary monitor.
Priya: Policy doc will include staged bump sequence (5%, 15%, hold at 40% manual review, then 100%), tenant cap, compliance checklist for private deployments, and an exceptions flow. I'll drop it in the policy repo by EOD Wed.
Maya: Timelines: policy doc 1w, runtime rollback PoC 2w, dashboards 1w, containment drill 3w. Owners: Priya (policy), Lina (runtime), Kevin (telemetry), Sam (SRE tests). Anyone object?
Lina: No objections. I'll mark runtime PR as draft and add unit tests for rollback idempotency.
Sam: I'll schedule a chaos drill for the staged flags and include a post-drill retro.
dev-bot: Action created: https://go/actions/pm/INC-2026-42/ai/42 assigned to Priya, Lina, Kevin, Sam
calendar-bot: Event created: "Staged-rollout containment drill" Thu 14:00 invites: Maya, Priya, Lina, Kevin, Sam
Maya: One more constraint: for Private/VPC deployments the default must remain off and we need an explicit compliance signoff before enabling auto-rollback. Priya please add to the policy.
Priya: Will do. Also adding a short checklist for auditors: backup plan, KMS key presence, and communication templates.
Omar: Nice. Let's track progress in the PM tracker and review in next week's postmortem sync. Thanks folks. :rocket:
